Violation is in the maintainer block, which this rule's own text explicitly extends to ("the later clauses extend it to <!-- maintainer --> blocks"). L51 (new this diff, `git show 95ff46a8` confirms it was added alongside the noun-run fix): "**Vocabulary (2026-08-26):** slide-4 heading and its last bullet swapped noun-*run* → *long-running session* / *session* per `vocabulary.md § The work` (§21b sweep finding; the refuters' kill over-read the 2026-08-14 notes, which authorize the beat, not the noun). Ran `sed -n '39,52p' <file> | grep -inE '\b(swapped|re-anchored|since|renamed|relocated)\b'` -> hits at L43 and L51. L51 contains three of the rule's own named transition tells at once: "swapped noun-run → long-running session" is the banned "X was changed to Y" shape verbatim (with an arrow instead of the word "to"); "re-anchored" is a relocation-family transition verb from the rule's own banned list; "the refuters' kill over-read the 2026-08-14 notes" narrates an internal review episode (a finding was filed, refuters wrongly killed it, it was later re-applied) that a future reader cannot resolve without git/session context — this is session biography, matching the rule's own banned example "restored after a judge caught it" almost exactly. Secondary, smaller instance in the same block, pre-existing from an earlier commit (5dd2806a, before this diff, so not part of the confirmed fix but caught by this full-class read): L43 "...`ironies-of-automation` follows it as the module's closing lecture (since 2026-08-25), and..." — "since" is explicitly named in the rule's transition-verb-tell list.
